quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking space, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and don't need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way road, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you and another driver arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light is a warning. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: At an intersection with no traffic signs or signals, what must you do?

options.text: Take the right-of-way carefully.
Wait for other drivers to signal you to go.
Slow down and yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to drivers who arrived before you.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no stop sign, yield sign, or signal, you must yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to drivers who arrived first.

questions.question: What can you do in a shared center lane on a two-way road?

options.text: Use it to pass other vehicles.
Use it as a regular lane during rush hour.
Drive in it as long as you are turning left.
Drive in it for no more than 300 feet before turning left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive in it for no more than 300 feet before turning left.
questions.explanation: A shared center lane is only for turning left. You cannot use it for passing or for driving more than 300 feet.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before it stops?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the pavement.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When riding a bicycle at night, how far must your white headlight be visible?

options.text: 300 feet.
400 feet.
500 feet.
600 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Your bicycle's white headlight must be visible for 500 feet at night. A red reflector must be visible for 600 feet at the rear. You can also use a flashing or steady red taillight in addition to the reflector.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. Drive slowly on slippery or poor roads to maintain control. Driving too fast on bad roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: Drive with the flow of traffic.
Limit your speed for the next 50 miles.
Speed limits are enforced for the next 50 miles.
The speed limit is 50 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed limit is 50 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum safe speed allowed on that road.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned when you make a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across lanes of traffic when turning.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking thirty minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green left arrow gives you the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who do not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: In a vehicle on a highway, it is:

options.text: Illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers in the passenger area.
Legal to drink if you are not the driver.
Legal to drink if you are driving but not drunk.
Illegal to drink from open alcohol, but legal to transport it in the passenger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers in the passenger area.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol in a vehicle on a highway. It is also illegal to have an open or partially used alcohol container in the passenger area. Open alcohol may only be stored in areas passengers do not use.
